Chub.name: Chub
Chub.description: The chub, also known as the European chub, is an adaptable fish from the carp family. It is robust and occurs in various types of water bodies.
Chub.habitat: Chub are extremely adaptable and live in rivers, streams, lakes and ponds. They prefer areas with current and shelters like roots or overhanging branches.
Chub.diet: Omnivore - feeds on insects, smaller fish, crustaceans, worms and plant matter
features: Orange-red belly and anal fins in older specimens
Chub.conservation: Not endangered - widespread and common species
Chub.funFact: Chub are true opportunists! They eat almost anything - from insects to fruits to small mice that fall into the water. That's why they're also called 'water pigs'.

Trout.name: Trout
Trout.description: The trout is a prized food and game fish from the salmon family. It is known for its tender, pink flesh and its preference for clean, oxygen-rich waters.
Trout.habitat: Trout prefer clear, cool and oxygen-rich waters. They live in streams, rivers and cool lakes, often in areas with strong currents.
Trout.diet: Predator - feeds on insect larvae, flying insects, crustaceans and smaller fish
features: Adipose fin between dorsal and tail fin
Trout.conservation: Varies by subspecies - brook trout partly endangered due to water pollution and river engineering
Trout.funFact: Trout have an amazing memory! They can remember feeding spots for months and learn to avoid artificial lures after being caught once.

Carp.name: Carp
Carp.description: The carp is one of the most famous freshwater fish and has been bred as a food fish for centuries. It is robust, long-lived and can reach impressive sizes.
Carp.habitat: Carp prefer warm, standing or slowly flowing waters with muddy bottoms and rich plant growth. They are found in ponds, lakes and river backwaters.
Carp.diet: Bottom feeder - feeds on worms, insect larvae, snails, mussels and plant material at the bottom of the water
features: Four barbels on the upper jaw
Long dorsal fin with serrated hard ray
Carp.conservation: Not endangered - widespread through stocking, wild forms partly endangered
Carp.funFact: Carp are incredibly intelligent and trainable! They can be trained to respond to bells to be fed. Some carp even recognize individual people and can distinguish faces. In Japan there are koi carp that have lived over 200 years!

Lamprey.name: Lamprey
Lamprey.description: The lamprey is a primitive, eel-like fish without jaws. It belongs to the oldest still living vertebrates and has hardly changed since 360 million years.
Lamprey.habitat: Lampreys live in rivers and streams with sandy or muddy bottoms. Some species migrate to the sea and return to freshwater to spawn.
Lamprey.diet: Depending on species: larvae filter small organisms from sediment, adult parasitic species attach to fish
Lamprey.size: 15-30 cm (brook lamprey), up to 120 cm (sea lamprey)
Lamprey.weight: 50-150 g (small species), up to 2.5 kg (sea lamprey)
features: Seven gill openings on each side
Eyes appear like nine (hence the name)
Lamprey.conservation: In Germany critically endangered to threatened with extinction - strictly protected by EU directives
Lamprey.funFact: Lampreys are living fossils! They existed before dinosaurs and have survived the last five mass extinctions. Their body structure is so successful that it has hardly changed.

Roach.name: Roach
Roach.description: The roach is a widespread freshwater fish from the carp family. It is easily recognizable by its characteristic red iris.
Roach.habitat: Roach live in standing and slowly flowing waters. They prefer lakes, ponds and rivers with rich plant growth.
Roach.diet: Omnivore - feeds on insect larvae, zooplankton, algae and aquatic plants
Roach.conservation: Not endangered - common species in European waters
Roach.funFact: Roach are very social fish and live in large schools that can comprise several thousand individuals.

Rudd.name: Rudd
Rudd.description: The rudd is a lively schooling fish from the carp family. It is often confused with the roach, but has bright red fins and a superior mouth.
Rudd.habitat: Rudd live in standing and slowly flowing waters with dense vegetation. They like to stay in middle water layers and between aquatic plants.
Rudd.diet: Omnivore with preference for plant food - eats algae, aquatic plants, insect larvae and zooplankton
Rudd.funFact: Rudd are true vegetarians among fish! While most carp fish are omnivores, rudd prefer plant food and can even eat larger plant parts. Their superior mouth is perfectly adapted to search for food at the water surface.

Tench.name: Tench
Tench.description: The tench is a peaceful bottom fish from the carp family. It is known for its olive-green coloration and its preference for weedy waters.
Tench.habitat: Tench prefer standing or slowly flowing waters with muddy bottoms and dense vegetation. They are often found in ponds, pools and weedy shore zones.
Tench.diet: Bottom feeder - feeds on insect larvae, snails, worms and plant material at the bottom of the water
features: Very small scales with thick mucus layer
Two short barbels on the mouth
Tench.conservation: Not endangered - stable populations in suitable waters
Tench.funFact: The tench is also called 'doctor fish'! In the past, people believed that its mucus had healing powers. In fact, the mucus layer contains antibacterial substances that protect it from infections.

Stickleback.name: Stickleback
Stickleback.description: The stickleback is a small but pugnacious fish with characteristic spines on its back. Despite its small size, it is known for its complex breeding behavior and aggressiveness.
Stickleback.habitat: Sticklebacks are very adaptable and live in lakes, ponds, streams, rivers and even brackish water. They prefer plant-rich shore zones.
Stickleback.diet: Small predator - feeds on zooplankton, insect larvae, small crustaceans and fish spawn
features: Three free-standing spines on the back
Bone plates instead of scales on the sides
Males during spawning season with red throat and blue back
Very large eyes in relation to body
Stickleback.conservation: Not endangered - very common and adaptable species
Stickleback.funFact: Stickleback males are amazing fathers! They build elaborate nests from plant material, attract several females to spawn and then guard the eggs alone. They fan fresh water to them with their fins and defend the nest aggressively against any intruder - even against much larger fish!

Zander.name: Zander
Zander.description: The zander is a popular predatory fish from the perch family. It is known for its tasty, firm flesh and its excellent hunting abilities.
Zander.habitat: Zander prefer larger, deeper lakes and slowly flowing rivers with sandy or gravelly bottoms. They often stay near the bottom.
Zander.diet: Predator - feeds mainly on smaller fish like roach, perch and ruffe
features: Sharp canine teeth in the mouth
Greenish-gray coloration with dark transverse bands
Zander.conservation: Not endangered - important commercial fish in European waters
Zander.funFact: Zander can see very well even in murky water. Their large eyes have a special layer that amplifies the available light - similar to cats!
